Vendored sources for dynarmic-sys.  Touch this file after editing anything
under vendor/; it is the only thing under vendor/ that the build script tells
Cargo to watch.

    removed    .git/, .github/, docs/  -- build inputs only

    Why a vendored tree and not a submodule: `merryhime/dynarmic`, the
    original, already 404s (D5).  yuzu-mirror is itself a mirror of a
    repository that disappeared, and a mirror of a dead upstream is exactly
    the kind of dependency that vanishes next.  A submodule would make a
    fresh clone depend on it still existing; a vendored tree does not.  It
    also satisfies Global Constraint 8 outright rather than conditionally:
    there is nothing to fetch, at build time or at test time.

    externals/ are vendored by upstream as git subtrees, not submodules, so
    the revision above pins them too.

boost/
    upstream   Boost 1.88.0, headers only
    licence    Boost Software License 1.0 (see boost/LICENSE_1_0.txt)
    contents   a 1,786-file subset, not all of Boost (which is 185 MiB)

    Boost is an *undeclared* dynarmic dependency.  The prior-art survey listed
    fmt / mcl / xbyak / zydis / robin-map and Boost was not in it; dynarmic in
    fact needs boost::icl (interval_set, interval_map -- code-cache
    invalidation ranges) and boost::variant (the IR terminal type).

    The subset is derived, not curated: see ../tools/derive_boost_subset.py.
    It is the transitive closure of what MSVC actually opened while building
    the pin, unioned with boost/preprocessor/** and
    boost/mpl/aux_/preprocessed/** in full, because those are reached through
    macro-built #include directives that no textual scan can follow and whose
    contents differ per compiler.

    Note for a future non-MSVC build: the closure was measured with MSVC.  Re-run
    the derivation script when adding a toolchain rather than guessing.
